FOREWORD

Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 12 May 1983, after the draft finalized by the Cosmetics Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. published in 1969 and subsequently reviewing this standard the Sectional separately the essential and optional was formed non-implementable for revision, only a single set of require-

0.2 This standard was originally Initially while revised in 1977. Committee had agreed to indicate requirements. Subsequently this Certification and therefore in this ments has been stipulated.

0.3 Isopropyl myristate is essentially a mixture of isopropyl ester of myristic acid and small amounts of isopropyl ester of lauric and palmitic acids. It is being increasingly used in the cosmetic industry because of its excellent emollient and solvent properties. Its intrinsic advantages are that it is colourless,,practically odourless and is not prone to oxidation. It has a very low degree of irritability and exhibits non-sensitizing properties. Isopropyl myristate imparts a characteristic non-greasy feel when used in creams, lotions, both oils and other cosmetics. 0.4 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been taken from specification No. 40 of 1967 `Isopropyl myristate', of the Toilet Goods USA and Specification No. 22 of 1958 `Isopropyl Association Inc, myristate', of the Toilet Preparations Federation Ltd, UK. 0.5 For the this standard purpose of deciding whether a particular is complied with, the final value, observed 3 requirement of or calculated,

A-5.2 Procedure - Weigh accurately about 3 g of the material in `tared platinum or silica dish. Slowly burn the material and finally ignite it in furnace at 600 f 25�C until all carbonaceous matter has disappeared. Cool in a desiccator and weigh. Repeat till constant mass is obtained. A-5.3.
